builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
summary: The method replaces additional cross-entropy pre-training of a limit-order-book generator with a short adversarial post-training stage: a WGAN critic evaluates free-running rollouts through the real matching engine and evolution strategies update rank-4 LoRA perturbations under a KL trust region. It costs under 50M training tokens and roughly 12 GPU-hours per seed, but presupposes an existing pre-trained LOB foundation model (a 48B-token pre-training budget), access to a non-differentiable matching engine, and online critic infrastructure. It can fail through reward hacking of the critic, as the paper's own analysis notes, and its gains are specific to market-simulation fidelity rather than general language-model quality.
rationale: The technique targets LOB market simulation for high-frequency trading and requires a pre-trained domain-specific foundation model and matching engine, so it lies outside the production scope of a general AI/ML engineer despite its modest compute cost.
technique: Adversarial post-training of LOB foundation models via WGAN and LoRA evolution strategies

claims.statement: The method replaces additional cross-entropy pre-training of a limit-order-book generator with a short adversarial post-training stage: a WGAN critic evaluates free-running rollouts through the real matching engine and evolution strategies update rank-4 LoRA perturbations under a KL trust region. It costs under 50M training tokens and roughly 12 GPU-hours per seed, but presupposes an existing pre-trained LOB foundation model (a 48B-token pre-training budget), access to a non-differentiable matching engine, and online critic infrastructure. It can fail through reward hacking of the critic, as the paper's own analysis notes, and its gains are specific to market-simulation fidelity rather than general language-model quality.

Adversarial post-training improves LOB-Bench realism by 17.6% (WS-21) and 17.0% (Mean-L1) on a held-out panel, and slows error accumulation over 500-message rollouts from 3.1x to 2.3x; controls with matched selection or compute show no improvement.
